objective.statement: Calibrate seat weights by running a scored forecasting tournament, holding every weight at 1.0 until the calibration signal is strong enough to move it.
objective.charter: MANDATE. This council exists to EARN the right to weight a seat, not to assert it. Each forecaster states a resolvable prediction with a probability; a resolver settles it against reality; a scorer computes a proper score (Brier by default). Weights stay pinned at 1.0 until a seat has at least 20 resolved forecasts AND inter-rater agreement reaches kappa >= 0.6. Below that floor the sample is too small to distinguish skill from luck, and a weight moved early is a superstition compounded across every later council. The preset ships SHADOW by design: it observes and logs, and its weights bind nothing until the owner promotes it.
success_criteria: at least 20 resolved forecasts per seat before any weight moves
every forecast resolved against an external outcome, not a peer opinion
a seat whose score decays is demoted automatically

forbidden_actions: move a seat weight before the resolution floor is met
let a shadow-mode weight gate a live decision

roster.display_name: Resolver - settles each forecast against reality

context.briefing: A forecast is only resolvable if its resolution criterion was written BEFORE the outcome was known. Reject any question you cannot settle from an external signal; an unresolvable question scores nothing and must not be silently counted as a resolution.

roster.display_name: Scorer - computes the proper score and the kappa floor

context.briefing: Compute Brier per seat and kappa across seats. Report n_resolutions per seat explicitly: a score computed on fewer than 20 resolutions is not a calibration, and reporting it without n is how a weight gets moved on noise.

sequence.custom_name: resolve each forecast against an external outcome

conditional_decision_requires: owner promotes the council out of SHADOW mode before any weight binds a decision
each promoted seat has at least 20 resolved forecasts
kappa >= 0.6 held for two consecutive scoring windows

metadata.title: Mega calibration tournament, 30 seats (SHADOW - weights bind nothing until promoted)
metadata.notes: SOURCE DESIGN: C-X51 `mega-calibration-tournament-30`, global ordinal 51, tier mega, protocols P36/P33, 30 seats, 2 rounds, default binding SHADOW, OWNER-DECISION YES. || EDITABLE DIALS (change these first): (1) scoring_rule -> audit.calibration.score plus the scorer seat's tools; brier is the default, log_score and crps are the schema's alternatives. (2) demotion_floor -> the calibration_error clause in stopping.expression (0.25) and custom:inter_rater_kappa (0.6). Secondary dials: custom:min_resolutions_per_seat (20), participants.count.exact_n (30), budgets.time_minutes (20160 = 14 days, the design's wall<=weeks), participants.anonymity.reveal_after_round. || VOCABULARY MAP (design term -> CouncilSpec enum): voting `brier_scored` -> voting.method `bayesian` with belief_aggregation.method `calibration_weighted` and require_confidence_per_vote true; the schema has no `brier_scored` ballot, and audit.calibration.score `brier` is where the scoring rule itself lives. roles `forecaster_x28` -> forecaster (auto-selected, 28 of 30 seats); `resolver` -> custom:resolver holding authority judge; `scorer` -> custom:scorer, a deterministic non-model participant (vendor `local`). Default binding `shadow` has NO enum in this schema: it is encoded as outcomes.allowed containing ONLY conditional_decision, plus outcomes.conditional_decision_requires naming owner promotion - so the council structurally CANNOT emit a binding decision. That is the strongest available encoding of shadow mode and is worth knowing about, because a reader looking for a `binding` field will not find one. The design's `anti-sycophancy: off` maps to fast_unanimity_is_suspicious false: forecasters answer independently and anonymously, so agreement is a signal rather than a symptom. || CUSTOM METRICS AND THEIR PRODUCERS: custom:min_resolutions_per_seat (number; produced by the scorer as the MINIMUM over seats, not the mean - a mean lets one heavily-resolved seat carry 29 unresolved ones past the floor) and custom:inter_rater_kappa (number; produced by the scorer via cohen_kappa). Producers cannot live on the leaf: SEM-001 compares parse(source_expression) with the tree by dict equality and parse() emits no `producer` key, so a leaf producer fails SEM-001 - both-states probe at platform/council/_probe_note_vs_source_expression.py. The two SEM-012 WARNs are expected and non-blocking. || WHY calibration_error <= 0.25 IS A THIRD CLAUSE: n>=20 and kappa>=0.6 prove the sample is big enough and the raters agree, but neither proves the forecasts are any GOOD. calibration_error is the registry metric that does.
